questions.prompt: Which of these is legislation rather than a voluntary framework or a certifiable standard?
questions.explanation: The EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) is law. NIST AI RMF is voluntary, ISO/IEC 42001 is a certifiable management-system standard, and model cards are a documentation practice.

questions.prompt: Which NIST AI RMF function is cross-cutting and covers policies, roles and accountability?
questions.explanation: Govern is cross-cutting. Map covers context and harms, Measure analyses and tests risks, Manage prioritises and acts on them.

questions.prompt: Under the EU AI Act, providers and deployers have different duties.
questions.explanation: True. Providers develop or place systems on the market; deployers use them. Their obligations differ.

questions.prompt: Since when have the EU AI Act's prohibitions and AI-literacy provisions applied?
questions.explanation: The Act entered into force on 1 August 2024; prohibitions and AI literacy have applied since 2 February 2025; GPAI model obligations since 2 August 2025. Always verify dates against the official timeline, because they have changed before.

questions.prompt: An HR team plans to use AI to screen job applicants in the EU. What is the right first step for the engineering team?
options: Decide alone that it is minimal risk
Flag it as a likely high-risk area (employment) and involve legal/compliance to classify it, then plan the evidence (risk management, logging, human oversight)
questions.explanation: Employment is a listed high-risk area. Engineers making legal classification calls alone is a listed mistake; they should provide evidence.

questions.prompt: Which engineering evidence supports a 'record-keeping' requirement? Select all that apply.
options: Logging tests showing each decision is traceable to model version and inputs
Retention and access rules for the logs
questions.explanation: Record-keeping needs traceable, retained, testable logs; brochures are not evidence.

questions.prompt: A model card reports 94% overall accuracy only. Why is this insufficient?
options: Model cards should include disaggregated results by relevant factors (groups, environments); overall metrics can hide poor subgroup performance
Model cards should only list the training data
questions.explanation: Mitchell et al. include factors and disaggregated quantitative analyses; overall-only metrics are a listed mistake.

questions.prompt: A chatbot built for product FAQs is repurposed to give credit-limit recommendations. What governance issue arises?
options: A change of intended use can change the risk classification and obligations; reassess before deployment
questions.explanation: Ignoring changes of intended use is a listed mistake.

options: Requirements for an AI management system (AIMS), similar in style to ISO/IEC 27001
questions.explanation: ISO/IEC 42001 defines a management system with leadership, policy, risk assessment, impact assessment, controls and audit; organisations can be certified against it.

coding.title: Model card completeness check
coding.prompt: Write `missing_sections(card)` where `card` is a dict of section name -> text. Required sections (Mitchell et al.) are: `model_details`, `intended_use`, `factors`, `metrics`, `evaluation_data`, `training_data`, `quantitative_analyses`, `ethical_considerations`, `caveats_and_recommendations`. Return the required sections that are missing or blank (only whitespace), in the order listed.

            "training_data", "quantitative_analyses", "ethical_considerations",
            "caveats_and_recommendations"]

def missing_sections(card):
    # Your code here
    pass
coding.solution:
REQUIRED = ["model_details", "intended_use", "factors", "metrics", "evaluation_data",
            "training_data", "quantitative_analyses", "ethical_considerations",
            "caveats_and_recommendations"]

def missing_sections(card):
    return [s for s in REQUIRED if not str(card.get(s, "")).strip()]
coding.explanation: Automating documentation checks in CI turns governance from a one-off document into a lifecycle gate: a release cannot ship with an empty intended-use or ethics section.
hints: Use `card.get(s, '')` and `.strip()` to detect blank text.

tests.name: Finds missing and blank
tests.code:
c={s:'x' for s in REQUIRED}
c['factors']='   '
del c['ethical_considerations']
assert missing_sections(c)==['factors','ethical_considerations'], missing_sections(c)

tests.name: Complete card
tests.code: assert missing_sections({s:'ok' for s in REQUIRED})==[] and len(missing_sections({}))==9

coding.title: Requirement-to-evidence traceability
coding.prompt: Write `untested(requirements, tests)` where `requirements` maps a requirement id to its theme (e.g. `{"R1": "record-keeping"}`) and `tests` is a list of dicts `{"id", "covers": [requirement ids], "status": "pass"|"fail"}`. Return a dict `{"no_evidence": [...], "failing": [...]}`: requirement ids with no covering test, and requirement ids with at least one failing covering test, each sorted.
coding.explanation: A traceability matrix links every requirement to engineering evidence. Gaps (no test) and red evidence (failing test) are exactly what an auditor or compliance reviewer will ask about first.
hints: Collect covered and failing requirement ids in sets.
Ignore ids that are not in the requirements dict.
